title: Fire Eye
paragraphs: Seeing the fighting pigs, the sister pig screamed.
“Buubuubu! Buubuubuubu! Buubu, buubu? Buubu.”
“I would never do such a thing! My big brother will come and save me! …Ah… It’s over. I really wish I hadn’t heard that.”

Father handed the sister pig over to the soldiers. The pigs were still making a fuss, but when their commotion caused Takt to writhe in pain, spewing blood from all over his body, they froze and began trembling. The sister pig was being condemned by the surrounding pigs, grunting accusations at her.
“What did that pig just say?”
Father watched the scene with an expression that could be interpreted as both exasperation and pity. When I called out to him, Itsuki answered.
“She said, ‘So what if a weak Seven Star Hero got killed? All the other heroes besides my brother are just trash anyway, so it doesn’t matter!’”
“They probably think strength justifies everything… I need to be careful of that mindset myself.”
“That’s true… Thinking about the way I and my companions lost control in Motoyasu-san’s stories, I can’t see it as someone else’s problem.”

Indeed, it is not just someone else’s problem. If we were to act selfishly, we would fall into the same trap. But we strive not to become like that. Especially when I think of the path Father walked in the first world, the difference is clear.

Did Father ever say that strength grants the right to do anything? Did he ever teach such a thing to the slaves in the village? No, what Father taught was that strength exists to protect others. Everyone in the village, including the Filolials, understood that.
“Strength justifies everything”… It reminds me of when Itsuki and his companions lost control on Cal Mira Island.
The scale might be different, but the core issue is the same. As for Ren, in the past loops, it felt like he naturally acted that way without realizing it.

If I recall correctly, Éclair was the one who taught Ren the true meaning of strength, wasn’t she? I can’t remember all the details, but strength exists to protect the weak. Hearing about the additional crimes of Takt’s pigs, it’s clear that strength does not exist to fulfill one’s ambitions. Perhaps it is because Father can only protect that he is the one best suited to convey this truth.
“I wish humans didn’t have to kill each other. But if this is the only way to protect, then we have no choice but to dirty our hands.”

Father muttered with a distant look in his eyes. Amidst the commotion caused by the pigs, Yuki-chan and the others underwent their class upgrades. The Filolial-sama, including Yuki-chan, completed a special class upgrade using the power of the feathers on their heads.
“Gaelion is done too—!”
Right after that, Rival completed his class upgrade using his own power. The assistant did the same.
“What should we do about Imia-chan? Should she take the same class upgrade as Sakura-chan and the others? Or go with Gaelion-chan’s path?”
“U-Um…”
The mole glanced back and forth between Sakura-chan and Rival. It must be a tough choice. From what I can see, the mole is quite indecisive. If it were me, I’d pick Sakura-chan without hesitation.
“U-Um, in the stories of the Spear Hero, w-which one did I choose?”
The mole looked at me and asked. She wanted to use it as a reference for her decision.
“I wouldn’t know. You didn’t seem to be fond of fighting in the first place, so I never asked.”
“Maybe she never even did a class upgrade.”
“Naofumi, you sure like making people choose tough decisions.”
“I just think it’s better if they choose for themselves.”
“How are they even different in the first place?”
Of course, there’s a difference. A Filolial-sama’s class upgrade is different from a normal class upgrade—it raises all stats. The dragon side? I wouldn’t know anything about that.
“I can only estimate, but I’d say Sakura-chan and the others have a slightly better stat boost. On the other hand, Gaelion-chan’s upgrade seems to focus more on increasing skills.”
“Um, if you go with Sakura’s path, it makes movement easier—”
“Is that advice from Fitoria-san?”
“Yeah. She’s actively giving advice so that Gaelion doesn’t steal more followers.”
Father was discussing with Sakura-chan and the large Filolial-sama. Then, Rival butted into the conversation. Don’t interrupt. Father is having an important discussion right now.
“Gaelion won’t lose when it comes to advice either! If you take Gaelion’s class upgrade, you’ll develop a stronger aptitude for magic!”
“So, in summary, Filolials lean more towards physical abilities, while dragons focus more on magic?”
“From a talent perspective, Filolial upgrades also seem to enhance dynamic vision and reflexes.”
“Yeah, something like that. It would make it easier for Imia-chan to fight too.”
“The future is magic! Let’s use chant magic to support Naofumi and the others!”

Sakura-chan and Rival started glaring at each other. Well then, I shall join in as well. As I got up, Ren and Itsuki stopped me. Lately, it feels like not only Father but also these two have come to understand me.
“Uu…”
“Don’t fight.”
“This is where I unleash the creative magic I devised last night before bed! Zweit Fire Eye!”
I unleashed a heat ray from my eyes toward Rival.
“W-What are you doing all of a sudden?!”
Rival was startled and averted his gaze.
Tch! I missed. Since chanting too long would have made it obvious, I kept it to Zweit level, but that backfired.
“Did you just shoot a heat ray from your eyes?!”
“I don’t know how long you actually spent making that spell before bed… but don’t mess around, Motoyasu!”
“That’s dangerous! Using magic just to win a staring contest?!”
Father and the others scolded me.
“What are you doing to Gaelion?!”
The assistant was fuming. I don’t care. Dragons are my enemies. Just because he protected Sakura-chan the other day doesn’t mean he can get carried away.
“As expected of you, Lord Motoyasu! You even defeated Gaelion in a staring contest! I should work hard to master this as well!”
“You don’t need to learn this! It’s such a pointless attack spell.”
Rival glared at Yuki-chan.
Another staring contest! This time, I won’t miss!
“Gaelion won’t lose either! A gaze infused with magic!”
Before I could fire my shot, Rival suddenly emitted a blinding flash from his eyes!
“M-My eyes! My eyes—!”
Since I was aiming and chanting, I got hit directly, and my vision blurred.
Ugh… what a savage dragon!
“What are they even doing…”
“He actually got the better of Motoyasu. Gaelion-san is quite something too.”
“Motoyasu was the one who struck first. He brought it upon himself.”
“Gaelion-chan’s instant counterattack was impressive, but… I feel like they’re channeling their efforts in the wrong direction. ‘Wasted talent’ really fits here.”
Father gave a wry smile. I wish he’d be a little more considerate.
“If I recall correctly, to learn the Liberation-class spells Motoyasu can use, one needs to master Dragon Vein Magic, right?”
“That’s right. And to do so, one must receive the ‘Blessing of the Dragon’—a truly repugnant thing.”
At first, I felt disgusted as well. I remember Rival reluctantly casting the spell on me too. Without Father’s authority, I wouldn’t have been able to learn Dragon Vein Magic.
“Then, we’ll need to receive Gaelion-chan’s blessing too. After that, we’ll have to study magic even more.”
“Using orbs to learn it might be an option, but taking the easy way out won’t work… If we want to surpass such formidable individuals, it’s something we’ll have to do.”

“Just like with weapon enhancements, if you try to get stronger the easy way, you’ll end up like those guys screaming over there. Especially since Naofumi specializes in support magic, I’m interested in seeing how he could use his hero’s power to enhance it even further.”
Ren’s words reminded me—our Level Reset work is still ongoing. Ignoring the pigs as much as possible, we continued our discussion.
